# Test fixtures

Every file here is **generated by `generate.py`** and is original synthetic
content owned by this repository. No published paper, third-party document, or
personal data is redistributed — that is a licensing requirement, not a
preference: the test suite has to be reproducible by anyone who clones the repo.

Regenerate everything (and re-verify its routing classification):

```bash
npm run fixtures
# or: python tests/fixtures/generate.py
```

`generate.py` imports the plugin's own `lib/docprobe.py` and asserts that each
fixture routes the way the tests expect. If a change to the column-geometry
heuristics breaks that, regeneration fails loudly rather than silently leaving
fixtures that no longer test what they claim.

## What each file is for

| File | Branch it exercises |
|---|---|
| `two-column.pdf` | Real two-column geometry → `columns: multi-column`, est 2 → `pdf_markdown` |
| `single-column.pdf` | One text box → `columns: single-column` → `markitdown` / `pypdf` |
| `scanned.pdf` | JPEG-only page, zero text layer → `render_to_png + read_image` |
| `sample.docx` | ZIP container containing `word/document.xml` → `docx` |
| `sample.xlsx` | ZIP container containing `xl/workbook.xml` → `xlsx` |
| `sample.pptx` | ZIP container containing `ppt/presentation.xml` → `pptx` |
| `sample.png` | Image magic bytes → `read_image` |
| `sample.rtf` | RTF header → `read` |
| `sample.csv` / `.json` / `.html` / `.txt` | Text-ish containers, extension-mapped |
| `magic-ole2.doc` | OLE2 header (legacy binary Office) → `ole2` |
| `magic-plain.zip` | ZIP without any Office part → `zip` |

## A note on the `magic-*` fixtures

`magic-ole2.doc` is **header-only** (the 8-byte OLE2 signature plus padding) and
`magic-plain.zip` is an empty-ish zip. They are deliberately *not* valid
documents.

That is the honest minimal input for the rule they test: `doc_route` classifies
by file header, never by opening the document. Building a 512-byte file that
genuinely is not a Word document keeps the fixture small and makes it obvious
that only the magic-byte path is under test. Do not "fix" them into real Office
files, and do not use them to test conversion — conversion is not what they
cover.

## Binary fixtures are committed on purpose

The PDFs, Office files and PNG are checked in so that `npm test` works on a bare
clone with no Python, no PyMuPDF and no network. The integration tests skip
themselves when PyMuPDF is absent; the unit tests never need any of this.

`.gitattributes` marks these files `binary` so git never rewrites their bytes,
and `linguist-vendored` so they stay out of the repository's language stats.
